title: Journal reservation bounds the measured journal bytes including the signal history and temporary records

fixture.reservation: restart = max(2(B+S), S+2(B+G)) + 64 KiB + 16*(steps//depth+2) + 2*(512+256*(arrays+1)) bytes, with B the bank bytes, S the signal history bytes and G the gradient bytes, reported as restart_signal_history_bytes and restart_journal_metadata_bytes
fixture.journal: tests/test_streamed_restart.py: durable journal with every-block records, coexisting forward and backward records, existing records from an earlier run, stale .tmp leftovers

reference_method: measured peak bytes under the journal directory, sampled while a .tmp record is being written and at every removal, compared with the reservation charged to the volume

observables.name: peak_journal_bytes
observables.definition: largest total size of the journal directory observed during the run

observables.name: reservation_bytes
observables.definition: restart reservation charged by the planner for the same run

observables.name: existing_bytes_credit
observables.definition: bytes of records already present that are counted toward the reservation, excluding .tmp leftovers

acceptance.bound: peak_journal_bytes <= reservation_bytes for every recorded fixture, including the moment a .tmp record coexists with its predecessor
acceptance.space_check: a journal directory whose free space is below the reservation is refused before the run starts
acceptance.leftovers: .tmp leftovers are removed only directly under the journal directory, are not credited as existing bytes, and a pointer naming a record outside the journal is refused
acceptance.shared_volume: when journal and banks share a volume the two reservations are summed against it
acceptance.source_of_limits: byte accounting is exact; no tolerance

applicability: Durable restart journals on local volumes; network shares and quota-managed volumes are not measured.
not_yet_covered: power-loss durability (only process-kill consistency is exercised)
